title: Caesar Salad
subtitle: Cos lettuce with anchovy dressing, croutons, and Parmesan
excerpt: Crisp leaves of cos lettuce coated in a sharp, garlicky anchovy dressing, scattered with golden croutons and shavings of Parmesan. One of the great salads, barely changed from the original.

recipe.sourceNotes: Caesar salad was created by Caesar Cardini, an Italian immigrant restaurateur working in Tijuana, Mexico, in the early 1920s. Cardini opened a restaurant just across the US-Mexico border to serve American customers during Prohibition, and the salad is said to have been improvised from pantry ingredients during a busy Fourth of July weekend when supplies were running low. The original recipe contained romaine lettuce, garlic, croutons, Parmesan, boiled egg, Worcestershire sauce, and lemon juice; anchovies were not in the first version but became a standard addition. The dressing is now typically made with raw or soft-boiled egg yolk and is one of the first emulsified dressings most home cooks encounter. The dish became internationally popular through mid-century American restaurant culture. The gluten-free designation applies to the salad without croutons.

content.text: The dressing must be sharp: this salad should taste strongly of lemon, anchovy, and garlic. A timid dressing produces a bland salad. Use the inner leaves of the cos only: the pale, crisp hearts have the right texture and do not wilt under the dressing. Dress the leaves at the very last moment and toss thoroughly so every leaf is coated. The croutons should be made from bread that is at least a day old: fresh bread croutons are soft in the centre and do not stay crisp.

items.preparation: inner leaves only, torn or left whole

content.text: Make the croutons: toss the torn bread in olive oil, season, and bake at 200 C / fan 180 C for 10 minutes until golden and crisp. Set aside.

Make the dressing: pound the anchovies and garlic together to a paste. Whisk in the egg yolk, Dijon mustard, and Worcestershire sauce. Add the lemon juice. Whisk in the olive oil in a thin stream until emulsified. Season.

Toss the lettuce leaves in the dressing to coat every leaf. Add the croutons and two-thirds of the Parmesan and toss again. Transfer to a serving dish or plates and scatter the remaining Parmesan over the top.
